statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows moderate correlations (r ≈ 0.3–0.5) between resting HRV and stress reactivity; sensor noise floors are well-characterized for commercial PPG/EDA, allowing power analysis.
minimum_data_needed: Resting 5-min supine RMSSD and HF-HRV for each subject
Phasic EDA reactivity (peak amplitude, SCR frequency) to standardized lab stressor (e.g., TSST)
Continuous wearable PPG/EDA during stressor with synchronized ground-truth stress labels
Per-subject sensor noise floor estimates (PPG SQI at rest, EDA baseline noise variance)
Subject-level stress classifier predictive entropy and false negative rate
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Subjects in the lowest tertile of resting RMSSD will show ≥2× higher false negative rate and ≥1.5× higher predictive entropy than subjects in the highest tertile, after controlling for age, sex, and fitness.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: No significant difference in false negative rate or predictive entropy across RMSSD tertiles (p > 0.05, equivalence test with Δ = 0.2 SD), or the correlation between RMSSD and uncertainty is fully mediated by sensor noise floor (indirect effect 95% CI excludes zero while direct effect includes zero).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Compute per-subject FNR and predictive entropy from stress classifier. 2) Fit linear mixed model: uncertainty ~ RMSSD_tertile + EDA_reactivity + age + sex + VO2max + (1|device_unit). 3) Test RMSSD_tertile contrast (low vs. high) with Holm-Bonferroni correction. 4) Mediation analysis: RMSSD → sensor_noise_floor → uncertainty. 5) Power: N=120 achieves 80% power to detect f²=0.15 at α=0.05.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Requires standardized stressor to ensure comparable physiological demand; exclude beta-blocker/anticholinergic users; measure sensor noise floor per session per subject.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Published PPG signal quality differences across Fitzpatrick skin types show Cohen's d ≈ 0.6–0.8 for green-light PPG; EDA impedance differences across stratum corneum thickness show similar magnitudes.
minimum_data_needed: Spectrophotometric melanin index at 650nm (forearm and wrist)
Stratum corneum thickness via confocal microscopy
Corneometry skin hydration values
Trichoscopy hair density counts at sensor site
Per-subject PPG signal quality index (SQI) and EDA contact impedance during standardized stress protocol
Subject-level classifier predictive entropy and calibration error
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Melanin index and stratum corneum thickness will each independently predict ≥15% of variance in predictive entropy (ΔR² ≥ 0.15) after controlling for motion artifact, ambient light, and device fit.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: In hierarchical regression, melanin index and stratum corneum thickness add no significant variance beyond motion artifact and device fit (ΔR² < 0.02, p > 0.05), or the association reverses direction when using multi-wavelength PPG (green + IR) that corrects for melanin attenuation.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Recruit stratified sample across Fitzpatrick I–VI (n≥20 per type). 2) Measure skin phenotypes and sensor metrics during controlled lab stressor. 3) Fit mixed model: entropy ~ melanin_index + corneum_thickness + hydration + hair_density + motion_var + strap_tension + (1|subject). 4) Test unique variance contribution of skin phenotypes via likelihood ratio test. 5) Repeat with multi-wavelength PPG features to test attenuation correction. 6) Power: N=120 achieves 80% power for f²=0.10 at α=0.05.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Must control ambient light and temperature; standardize sensor placement; exclude skin pathologies; use multi-wavelength PPG to isolate melanin effect from perfusion.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Circadian phase effects on cortisol and autonomic reactivity show medium effect sizes (η² ≈ 0.06–0.14); chronotype × time-of-day interactions on cognitive performance show similar magnitudes.
minimum_data_needed: Dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) or Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ) score for each subject
Timestamp of each stressor exposure relative to DLMO (hours since DLMO)
Salivary cortisol awakening response (CAR) magnitude
Continuous wearable HRV/EDA during stressors at varying circadian phases
Per-subject classifier stress probability outputs and ground-truth labels
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: The chronotype × circadian phase interaction will explain ≥10% of variance in subject-level calibration error (ECE); morning types will show ≥20% higher ECE for stressors >10h post-DLMO vs. <4h post-DLMO, with reverse pattern for evening types.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Adding circadian phase × chronotype interaction to a model predicting ECE does not significantly improve fit (ΔAIC > 2, p > 0.05), or the interaction effect disappears when time-of-day is added as an explicit feature to the classifier.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Measure DLMO in lab; collect 14-day free-living wearable + EMA data. 2) Bin stressors by hours since DLMO (4 bins). 3) Compute per-subject per-bin ECE and AUC. 4) Fit linear mixed model: ECE ~ chronotype * circadian_bin + sleep_duration + light_exposure + (1|subject). 5) Test interaction contrast with FDR correction. 6) Retrain classifier with time-of-day feature; compare ECE via paired bootstrap. 7) Power: N=80 with ≥5 stressors/bin achieves 80% power for f²=0.10.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: DLMO measurement essential; exclude shift workers and recent travelers; control prior light exposure; ensure stressor type balanced across circadian bins.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Emotion regulation effects on peripheral physiology are typically small (d ≈ 0.2–0.4); label-physiology decoupling may be subtle and require large samples to detect.
minimum_data_needed: Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) suppression and reappraisal subscale scores
State ERQ during each stressor epoch
Concurrent EMA subjective stress ratings (0–100 VAS)
Multi-modal wearable features (HRV, EDA, HR, respiration) during stress epochs
Per-subject classifier predictive entropy and label-physiology residuals
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Trait suppression score will correlate positively with predictive entropy (r ≥ 0.25) and label-physiology residual magnitude (r ≥ 0.25); reappraisal will correlate negatively (r ≤ -0.20).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Correlations between ERQ subscales and uncertainty metrics are non-significant (p > 0.05) and Bayes factors favor null (BF₀₁ > 3), or the association is fully mediated by interoceptive awareness (MAIA) such that direct effect of suppression on uncertainty is zero.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Administer ERQ and MAIA. 2) TSST with concurrent EMA (every 2 min) and wearable recording. 3) Compute per-subject predictive entropy and label-physiology residual (|EMA - predicted_stress|). 4) Fit SEM: suppression → label_physiology_residual → entropy; reappraisal → label_physiology_residual → entropy; control MAIA, anxiety, alexithymia. 5) Test indirect effects via bootstrap (5000 samples). 6) Power: N=150 achieves 80% power for r=0.25 at α=0.05.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Distinguish trait vs. state regulation; use multi-modal features; control baseline affect; consider regulation-aware labeling (separate labels for regulated vs. unregulated stress).

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Effect size depends on prevalence and stress-correlation of non-wear, which varies widely across populations and device types; no published estimates exist for stress-correlated non-wear bias magnitude.
minimum_data_needed: Accelerometer-detected non-wear episodes (timestamp, duration) for ≥14 days
Event-contingent and random EMA stress ratings during wear periods
Retrospective EMA stress recall for non-wear periods (prompted at next wear)
Per-subject observed stress classifier uncertainty during wear
Imputed ground-truth stress time series (multiple imputation with stress-correlated missingness model)
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Subjects with >30% non-wear during high-stress EMA (top quartile) will show ≥25% downward bias in observed predictive entropy compared to imputed ground-truth entropy; low-stress non-wear subjects will show ≥15% upward bias.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Pattern-mixture models show missingness is ignorable (MAR): observed stress distribution during wear does not differ by non-wear group (KS test p > 0.05), and retrospective recall during non-wear shows no association with non-wear timing (logistic regression OR 95% CI includes 1).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Detect non-wear via accelerometer (SD < 0.01g for >20 min). 2) Collect random + event-contingent EMA (6x/day). 3) At re-wear, prompt retrospective stress for non-wear windows. 4) Compute observed per-subject entropy (wear only) and imputed entropy (multiple imputation with stress-predictive missingness model). 5) Fit mixed model: entropy_bias ~ non_wear_stress_correlation + total_non_wear + (1|subject). 6) Sensitivity analysis: vary MNAR assumptions via δ-adjustment. 7) Minimum N=100 with ≥20% non-wear.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Requires retrospective recall validation; use accelerometer to distinguish non-wear from sedentary wear; test pattern-mixture and selection models for informative missingness.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: RSA coupling strength explains 30–50% of HF-HRV variance; unmeasured respiration confounding of HRV stress reactivity shows medium effects in controlled studies (η² ≈ 0.08–0.12).
minimum_data_needed: Concurrent respiration (thoracic impedance or respiratory inductance plethysmography) and ECG/PPG during paced breathing (0.25 Hz) and free-living stress
RSA coupling coefficient: HF-HRV power per unit respiratory depth (ms²/L)
Vagal tone index (HF-HRV during controlled breathing)
HRV stress reactivity (ΔRMSSD, ΔHF from baseline to stressor)
Per-subject classifier predictive entropy for HRV-only model
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: RSA coupling coefficient will correlate negatively with HRV-only classifier entropy (r ≤ -0.35); adding respiration features to classifier will reduce entropy for weak couplers (lowest tertile) by ≥30% but not for strong couplers.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: RSA coupling coefficient shows no correlation with HRV-only classifier entropy (|r| < 0.15, p > 0.05), or respiration-augmented classifier does not differentially improve uncertainty for weak vs. strong couplers (interaction p > 0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Paced breathing protocol (0.25 Hz, 5 min) to compute RSA coupling coefficient. 2) TSST with concurrent respiration + wearable. 3) Train HRV-only and HRV+respiration classifiers. 4) Compute per-subject entropy for both. 5) Fit mixed model: entropy ~ coupling_tertile * model_type + fitness + (1|subject). 6) Test interaction. 7) Mediation: coupling → HRV_reactivity → entropy. 8) Power: N=90 achieves 80% power for interaction f²=0.10.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Must measure respiration concurrently; paced breathing for coupling assessment; exclude respiratory disorders; test free-breathing vs. stress breathing patterns.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Wear tightness effects on PPG signal quality show large within-subject effects (d > 0.8); between-subject variability in habitual tightness produces measurable heteroscedasticity in feature distributions.
minimum_data_needed: Wrist circumference (mm) and bone prominence (ultrasound)
Objective strap tension (pressure sensor integrated in strap) during wear
Self-reported tightness preference (visual analog scale)
PPG SQI and EDA contact impedance during standardized activity protocol (rest, walk, stress)
Per-subject stress classifier predictive entropy and feature distribution moments
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Strap tension will show U-shaped relationship with predictive entropy (quadratic term p < 0.01); optimal tension minimizes entropy. Wrist circumference × tension interaction will explain ≥12% of entropy variance.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Quadratic tension term non-significant (p > 0.05) and entropy monotonic in tension, or same subject wearing same device at same measured tension shows entropy variance > between-tension variance (ICC < 0.3).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Instrument strap with pressure sensor. 2) Lab protocol: rest, walk, TSST at 3 randomized tension levels (loose, medium, tight). 3) Measure PPG SQI, EDA impedance, entropy per condition. 4) Fit mixed model: entropy ~ tension + tension² + wrist_circ * tension + bone_prominence + activity + (1|subject). 5) Test quadratic and interaction terms. 6) Cross-validate personalized calibration (subject-specific tension offset) vs. population model. 7) Power: N=60 with 3 tensions achieves 80% power for quadratic f²=0.15.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Objective tension measurement essential; test dynamic tension changes during activity; control device model and strap material; exclude vascular pathology.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Allostatic load composites correlate with blunted stress reactivity (r ≈ -0.3 to -0.5); feature dynamic range compression and class separation reduction show medium effects in clinical populations.
minimum_data_needed: Validated allostatic load index (≥6 biomarkers: hair cortisol, CRP, HbA1c, SBP/DBP, waist-hip ratio, HDL, plus optional DHEA-S, fibrinogen)
Acute stress reactivity (HRV, EDA, cortisol) to TSST
Free-living wearable feature time series (≥7 days) with ground-truth stress labels
Per-subject feature dynamic range (max-min HRV/EDA during stress vs. baseline)
Per-subject class separation (Mahalanobis distance between stress/non-stress feature clusters)
Per-subject classifier predictive entropy
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Allostatic load index will correlate positively with predictive entropy (r ≥ 0.35) and negatively with class separation (r ≤ -0.35); feature dynamic range will mediate ≥50% of the allostatic load → entropy association.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Allostatic load index shows no association with entropy (p > 0.05) after controlling for age, medication, and comorbidities, or signal quality metrics (PPG SQI, EDA impedance) fully mediate the association (direct effect 95% CI includes zero).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Collect allostatic load biomarkers (fasting blood, hair, anthropometrics). 2) TSST for acute reactivity. 3) 14-day free-living wearable + EMA. 4) Compute per-subject dynamic range, class separation, entropy. 5) Fit SEM: allostatic_load → dynamic_range → class_separation → entropy; control age, sex, meds, comorbidities. 6) Test mediation via bootstrap. 7) Stratify by allostatic load tertiles; compare calibration curves. 8) Power: N=120 achieves 80% power for r=0.35.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Allostatic load requires ≥6 biomarkers; longitudinal design preferred for causality; test personalized baselines; exclude acute illness and ANS-affecting medications.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: EMA reactivity effects are typically small (d ≈ 0.1–0.3); interoceptive awareness moderation of reactivity is an understudied interaction likely requiring large samples.
minimum_data_needed: Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) score and heartbeat counting task accuracy
EMA prompt timestamps and stress ratings (random + event-contingent)
Continuous wearable physiology (HRV, EDA) in 5-min windows pre- and post-EMA prompt
Per-subject classifier predictive entropy for pre-EMA vs. post-EMA epochs
Expected calibration error (ECE) for pre-EMA vs. post-EMA epochs by awareness group
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: High awareness (MAIA top tertile) will show ≥15% lower predictive entropy but ≥20% higher ECE (overconfidence) for post-EMA epochs vs. pre-EMA; low awareness will show no pre/post difference in entropy or ECE.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: No pre/post EMA difference in entropy or ECE for either awareness group (paired t-test p > 0.05, equivalence Δ = 0.1 SD), or high awareness shows lower ECE (better calibration) post-EMA, indicating improved label accuracy not contamination.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Measure MAIA and heartbeat counting accuracy. 2) 14-day EMA (6 random + stress-contingent prompts/day) with continuous wearable. 3) Define pre-EMA (-5 to 0 min) and post-EMA (0 to +5 min) windows. 4) Compute entropy and ECE per subject per window. 5) Fit mixed model: entropy ~ awareness_tertile * window + prompt_type + (1|subject). 6) Test interaction. 7) Repeat for ECE. 8) Control prompts (non-stress questions) to isolate attention effect. 9) Power: N=150 achieves 80% power for interaction f²=0.06.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Include control (neutral) EMA prompts; habituation period ≥7 days; randomize prompt timing relative to stressors; measure physiological response to prompt itself.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Ignoring hierarchical structure in multilevel data produces large calibration biases; simulation studies show coverage probability deviations of 20–40% for high-variability subjects when random effects are omitted.
minimum_data_needed: ≥50 stress epochs and ≥50 non-stress epochs per subject (wearable features + ground-truth labels)
Subject-specific stressor type/intensity variation
Flat (pooled) classifier predictive distributions (mean, variance) per epoch
Hierarchical (mixed-effects) classifier predictive distributions per epoch
Per-subject prediction interval coverage probability (nominal 95%) for both models
Per-subject expected calibration error (ECE) for both models
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Flat model 95% prediction intervals will achieve <85% coverage for high-variability subjects (top residual variance quartile) and >98% coverage for low-variability subjects (bottom quartile); hierarchical model will achieve 93–97% coverage for both groups.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: Flat model coverage probability does not differ significantly across subject variability quartiles (χ² test p > 0.05), or hierarchical model shows no improvement in coverage calibration (Δcoverage_bias < 2%, p > 0.05 via paired bootstrap).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: 1) Collect ≥100 epochs/subject across varied stressors. 2) Fit flat logistic regression (or RF) and hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression with random intercepts, slopes (stressor intensity), and AR1 residuals. 3) Compute per-subject 95% prediction interval coverage and ECE via leave-one-subject-out CV. 4) Fit mixed model: coverage_bias ~ subject_residual_variance_quartile * model_type + (1|subject). 5) Test interaction. 6) Compare log-likelihood and WAIC. 7) Power: N=80 subjects with 100 epochs achieves >95% power for large interaction.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Requires multilevel modeling framework (Stan/brms or lme4); use subject-level CV folds; test random intercepts, slopes, AR1; compare Bayesian vs. frequentist hierarchical models.
